answer: Admission runs through an order book. A key posts a firm two-sided quote on its output, escrowed at twenty times quoted value, live all epoch; unhit quotes earn nothing. New keys sell at the unrated bid, a forty percent haircut shrinking with graded epochs. A thousand clones fetch a thousand haircuts, and across that horizon cannot pull quotes as price turns: their own selling walks the book down, marking escrow lower while an ocean of keys is absorbed at rising cost. Boundary: with one honest maker absorbing flow, spread covers risk and only the haircut stands. A trellis of prices, not names.
